To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the critical temperature of nuclear matter, Tc, and its equation of state, dTc/d rho s, can be determined from heavy ion collisions.

the limiting temperature of nuclear matter in heavy ion collisions is 16.6+2.0-1.6 MeV and that the compressibility of nuclear matter is 200+/-40 MeV, which is consistent with the value derived from giant monopoles.
the limiting temperature of nuclear matter is Tc=16+/-1 MeV and that K/m*1/2 rho s=0.15+/-0.01 MeV, which is consistent with the value determined by the giant monopole resonances in nuclei.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the properties of nuclear matter in the vicinity of the critical point.
the properties of hot and dense matter.
the equation of state and the properties of nuclear matter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the limiting temperatures observed in the experiments are in agreement with the theoretical model correlations and the experimental giant monopole data.
Tc, rho s, and (K/m*)-1/2 rho s-1/3 are all determined by the same underlying physics, namely the nuclear equation of state, and are all in good agreement with theoretical calculations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a) the limiting temperature in heavy ion collisions is the critical temperature Tc, b) the compressibility modulus of nuclear matter at Tc is K=220 MeV and the incompressibility of excited nuclei at Tc is in the range 220 MeV < K < 270 MeV, and c) the effective mass of nuclear matter is m* = 1.0 m.
the compressibility of nuclear matter is not very well constrained.
the limiting temperature of infinite nuclear is a measure of the compressibility modulus and the effective mass of the nucleon.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the limiting temperature in heavy-ion collisions can provide a new tool for studying the equation of state and compressibility of nuclear matter.

a combination of experimental and theoretical results on limiting temperatures and the compressibility of nuclear matter provides an independent determination of K that is in excellent quantitative agreement with the giant monopole value.

the limiting temperatures observed in heavy-ion collisions are consistent with the critical temperatures of infinite nuclear matter, which in turn is consistent with the compressibility modulus of moderately excited nuclei.
